reference.notes:
`withBase` and `withoutBase` now only count the base as present when the character right after it is a boundary: end of string, `/` or `?`. The full suite passes: 17 files and 579 tests, including both new suites and all the existing tests.

`src/utils.ts` had no bodies throwing `not implemented`, so I changed the two existing functions. In both, the `input.startsWith(_base)` check now calls a new private helper, `_hasBase(input, _base)`. It returns true only if `input` starts with the base and the next character is missing, `/` or `?`. It isn't exported, so the public interface is unchanged, and nothing else in either function changed. The edit is only in `src/utils.ts`.

As a result, `withBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin")` now gives `/admin/admin-dashboard`, and `withoutBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin")` returns the input unchanged instead of `/-dashboard`.
